decisions.reason: As a very recent, low-risk extension of the core hardware range in a growing market, it is worth keeping on offer until demand becomes clearer.
A handle family fits the firm's broad system portfolio and can be retained cheaply while management learns whether architects and project buyers adopt it.
Although another close-to-core design variant may face portfolio overlap, there is still too little evidence after launch to justify abandoning the option already created.
This design product is near the established business and likely inexpensive to keep listed, so the firm would wait for more market feedback before pruning it.
Because this lever-handle family supports the firm's breadth strategy and probably shares components and channels with existing products, keeping it open is the better option for now.
The electronic access system is strategically aligned with the firm's move toward digital building solutions, so management would be especially reluctant to withdraw it only shortly after launch.
